feedback.finish: Coal, oil and gas are all fossil fuels.

atoms.b: Fossil fuels like coal, oil and gas come from the ((++Earth moon)).
Fossil fuels are burned to release ((++energy sunlight)). This energy powers everything from cars to the heating inside your home.

When they are burned, fossil fuels also release ((++carbon_dioxide silver)), which is very bad for the environment. Carbon dioxide ((++heats cools)) the planet, causing global warming and climate change.

atoms.a: Cars are not powered by fossil fuels.

feedback.finish: The petrol and diesel that power cars are fossil fuels.

feedback.end: Cars release carbon dioxide, carbon monoxide and other toxins into the atmosphere.

atoms.a: Cars are good for the environment.

feedback.end: As they release toxins, cars are very bad for the environment. If you can, it is always better to avoid using cars!

instruction.text: Select the three ways to get to school that are least harmful to the environment.

feedback.end: Walking and cycling are the best ways to get to school as they are pollution-free. Taking public transport is another option that is less harmful to the environment as it reduces the number of cars on the road.

atoms.b: When fossil fuels are burned, the heat they create is transformed into ((++energy food)). This means that using energy furthers the ((++negative positive)) effects caused by fossil fuels.
In our homes, we use energy for lots of electrical appliances. Energy is also needed for central heating and pumping ((++water orange_juice)).
To help protect the environment, we should try to use as little energy as possible. We can do this by ((++reducing increasing)) the amount of water and electricity we use.

instruction.text: Match each picture to the way to help the environment.

a.sound: Walk to school instead of using a car.
Have a shower instead of a bath to save water.
Switch off the light when you are not in the room to save energy.
